senses.sense_definition: To pay off a debt or liability gradually through regular installments.

examples.text: The company decided to <w>amortize</w> the loan over a period of twenty years.
It is often easier to <w>amortize</w> large debts by making small monthly payments.

senses.sense_definition: To distribute the computational cost of an algorithm over many operations to reduce the average time per operation.

examples.text: We can <w>amortize</w> the cost of resizing the array by doubling its capacity only when necessary.
The algorithm is efficient because we <w>amortize</w> the expensive operations across many cheap ones.

senses.sense_definition: To transfer property into mortmain, typically to a religious or charitable institution.

examples.text: In medieval times, it was common for landowners to <w>amortize</w> their estates to the church.
The king restricted the right to <w>amortize</w> land to prevent the church from accumulating too much wealth.

traits.comment: Refers to historical legal practices regarding land ownership.
